summary: Tools in P/sfix/tools (git, HEAD 7d5dab2, status clean). Sentence identity no longer depends on mask labels, backticks, articles, numbers, printer output, member names, comment facts or bold step leads. One template now gives one id: the 297 old sentence ids map to 227, and every one of the 227 has a verdict. A word is masked as a model name only where the model supplied it. That is learned per unit template from how the word varies across the 21 variations, with the language under review left out of the learning. It is checked by 5 new masking controls (both modes): v3.2 fails 6 of those 10 runs, v3.3 passes all 10. rekey.js maps every record keyed by a class or sentence id through class occurrences. It was run for the nine languages and tested on a copy of the lua port. After it, all nine one commands PASS. The before/after table moves only by re-key merges and splits, plus 10 classes I recorded by hand and listed below. The one command now also fails on a stale build and on a stale hand record. Self-test: 203 controls, 0 failed, 1 moved. The moved one is go-tut-step4-dropped from scratch: it passed in v3.2 only because of the bold-lead artefact. That is a finding: a dropped sentence that only go's result style prints leaves no trace from scratch.

requests_for_shared.request: Mark, in what shared code prints, where a model name (an entity's or a field's name) is substituted
requests_for_shared.why: The tools learn model slots from how a word varies across the 21 variations. That cannot see a name a template only ever receives as one entity ('listing planet records, loading a planet' in the full CRUD tutorial line, `planet_id`, 'listing console records'), so those stay literal. It is conservative, but the identity then holds model names.
requests_for_shared.smallest_change: A zero-width marker around each model name that ReadmeQuick.ts, ReadmeRef.ts and runtimeprose.ts substitute, e.g. a helper modelName(x) that a docs-only build option renders as '⁣x⁣' and that a normal build leaves out. The tools would then mask exactly those.

requests_for_shared.request: Have runtimeprose.ts print facts in code comments with the same delimiters it uses in prose, or record which comment words are facts
requests_for_shared.why: listComment strips the collection's backticks (runtimeprose.ts:170), and carries() and failsShort print ok, err, nullValue and errSlot raw. The tools now find these through a union of every provider's values at named slot paths (ident.js COMMENT_PATHS), so a new slot path in a comment will be missed until the list is updated.
requests_for_shared.smallest_change: Keep the backticks in many() for comments, or export the list of fact paths each comment helper substitutes.

requests_for_shared.request: Fix the false sentences in shared code
requests_for_shared.why: The 5 sentences rb and lua print and that are now marked false, plus the 2 false ones elsewhere (7 false ids in all), are accepted in every reference language by rule or hand records and counted on each screen. A port cannot have them matched and must record them by hand.
requests_for_shared.smallest_change: As the reviewers' fix entries in results/s3b-sentences.txt say (ReadmeQuick.ts:79/82, ReadmeRef.ts:185, 209-212, 255-263, 344-345, and ts Config makeFeature).

for_ports:
For each port L in {perl, swift, ocaml, lua}, with W the port's workspace (W/tools = the v3.2 tools holding the port's records, W/sdkgen, W/out). Tested on a copy of lua; the only difference was that lua has no normalizers/lua.js.

```sh
export PATH=/opt/node24/bin:$PATH
S=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f1977c62-4748-5872-8f72-6f448dbac3f1/scratchpad/design/proto2/sfix
cp -a $S/tools W/tools-v33 && rm -rf W/tools-v33/.git W/tools-v33/review
for d in counts purity-allow; do [ -f W/tools/$d/L.json ] && cp W/tools/$d/L.json W/tools-v33/$d/; done
[ -f W/tools/normalizers/L.js ] && cp W/tools/normalizers/L.js W/tools-v33/normalizers/
node W/tools-v33/rekey.js --clone W/sdkgen --old W/out/old --new W/out/new --lang L --from W/tools --to W/tools-v33 --dry
node W/tools-v33/rekey.js --clone W/sdkgen --old W/out/old --new W/out/new --lang L --from W/tools --to W/tools-v33 --json W/rekey-L.json
W/tools-v33/portcheck.sh W/sdkgen W/out L
node W/tools-v33/rekey.js --clone W/sdkgen --old W/out/old --new W/out/new --lang L --from W/tools-v33
```
- The second rekey run must print 'already keyed ... nothing changed'.
- rekey exits 1 when something is listed for a person (CONFLICT, UNSOURCED, or a hand entry that could not be carried). Decide those in W/tools-v33/hand/L.json.
- Expect 5 open classes, the false-verdict sentences. Record them as hand/rb.json records them (the reference class's outcome plus the reason), or wait for the shared fix.
- If W/sdkgen was rebuilt after the last generation, portcheck now names any STALE BUILD file.

For the merging engineer:
- copy each port's re-keyed hand/L.json, classes/L.json, counts/L.json, purity-allow/L.json (and normalizers/L.js) into sfix/tools, and add L to ported.json;
- run `for l in <nine + ports>; do tools/portcheck.sh <clone> <out> $l; done`;
- adding a learner can move a template's slots: if a language then shows RECOUNT or open classes, run `git -C tools worktree add <dir> <the commit before the merge>`, then `node tools/rekey.js --clone .. --old .. --new .. --lang $l --code <dir>` for each language (as P/sfix/logs/rekey2 and rekey3 did here), then `node tools/rekey.js --verdicts P/sentences/merged.json --clone .. --old .. --new .. --refs-from P/base32/tools --out tools/reviewed/sentences.json` and `node tools/sentences.js ...`;
- run the self-test with `--v32 P/base32/tools` as in the selftest field.
